criteria.description: No new test case over 1s; five runs, slowest per run with /proc/loadavg beside each, on PR head
criteria.note: re-measure. The only recorded measurement is qa.1:60, '145 ms slowest, five runs, load average 6.09'. It has one load figure, not /proc/loadavg beside each of the five runs, and no per-run slowest case. It was taken at head 625f92f5 (qa.1:24), before the QA cycle 1 and 2 commits that changed the new test files (head is bd986dc0). The criterion requires the PR head commit. qa.2 and qa.3 record no timing. The implementation report line (:71) is uncommitted evidence and does not count. The behaviour looks fine: the new tests are fast and the full suite passes.

criteria.description: Each new refusal has a mutation proof recorded in the QA report

members.member: extract no-block / empty-block / transcript-not-found / transcript-ambiguous / transcript-unreadable

criteria.note: The QA reports record 8 distinct mutation proofs (qa.1:118-123, qa.2:54-59, qa.3:44). The diff adds more refusals than that. No QA report records a revert-and-red proof for the outside-work-dir, not-an-array, missing, not-json, cases_file hash-mismatch, cases-and-cases_file or argv-entity refusals, nor for the extract refusals other than entity-escaped. The refusals have tests (security-probe-plan-cases-file.test.mjs:95, agent-reply-block.test.mjs:170), but the criterion asks for a recorded proof for each. qa.1:118 proves the byte copy, which is not a refusal.

criteria.description: bundle --check reports 0 problems; CI=true npm test passes
criteria.note: I ran 'command npm run bundle -- --check' on HEAD bd986dc0: 129 skills, 0 problems. I ran 'TMPDIR=/tmp CI=true npm test' on HEAD: 8001 tests, 7999 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped, exit 0. qa.3:56-57 records the same. .github/workflows/test.yml:58 runs npm test per PR. 'command' could not be prefixed to 'CI=true command npm test' in my shell, so I ran 'CI=true npm test'.

I ran 'python skills/create-skill/scripts/quick_validate.py skills/finalise' on HEAD: it passed and printed '✓ finalise'. qa.1:135 records the same run, and qa.2:71 records 'npm run validate -- skills/finalise/ # pass'. The criterion is a command outcome, not a behaviour a test can pin. Whether validate.yml runs it per PR was not checked.
